name.en: Fake eFlow text about an unpaid motorway toll

how.en: A text that claims to be from eFlow says you have an unpaid M50 or motorway toll, or even a “radar ticket”, and threatens penalties such as prosecution, a suspended licence or vehicle registration, extra charges or harm to your credit score. A link leads to a fake eFlow website asking for your card details. It works because many people really have driven through a toll recently.

text.en: A text says it is from eFlow or a toll operator.
It says you owe an unpaid toll and must pay by a deadline.
It threatens prosecution, penalties or your licence.
A link leads to a fake payment page for your card details.
eFlow: Our records show an outstanding M50 passage on your vehicle. Pay the €3.70 balance before midnight to avoid a €40 penalty and further enforcement: [link]

en: m50 toll text with a link
text saying i will be prosecuted for a toll
motorway toll text asking for card details
A link in a toll text: pay tolls only on eFlow’s official website, typed in yourself.
Threats of prosecution, licence suspension or credit score damage.
A sender number from outside Ireland.
Don’t click the link. Check your account on eFlow’s official website or app.
If you entered card details, call your bank straight away.

sources.title: Gardaí urge public to be vigilant over latest eFlow scam texts
